title: Workflows, agents and who owns the control flow

items.stem: Which question best separates a workflow from an agent in a system built around a language model?

options.text: Does the system call the language model more than once for a request?
Does the model or the program's code decide what happens after each step?
Is the system allowed to call outside tools such as a booking calendar?
Does the system remember earlier requests from the same student's visits?

items.stem: In your assistant, one model call reads each incoming message and labels it "booking" or "question". Code then sends it down one of two paths whose steps you wrote in advance. How should this design be described?

options.text: An agent, because the model's label decides which path the request takes
An agent, because the pipeline calls a model more than once per request
Neither, because a system with a model call in it cannot be a workflow
A workflow, because the model only picks among paths that the code defines

items.stem: Your sponsor's budget is counted in model calls, and you may assume every call costs the same. A fixed workflow handles one booking request with 2 model calls. An agent handling the same kind of request averages 5 tool requests and then a final answer, and each of those is one model call. Over 200 booking requests, how many more model calls does the agent use than the workflow?

Your team can afford to build only one part of the assistant as a fixed workflow. Which part is best suited to it, because its steps are known in advance and do not depend on what earlier steps return?

options.text: Booking a slot: check the calendar, check training, save it, then send a confirmation
Diagnosing a failing print, where each check chosen depends on what the last one found
Answering a hard question, where which manuals to search is not known beforehand
Planning a whole project, where the tasks and their order change as the student replies

items.stem: A teammate wants the booking steps built as an agent because "agents are more capable". The steps are always the same. In one or two sentences, give one reason, based on your budget or reliability, to build them as a fixed workflow instead.

Your booking agent is told in its prompt to check a student's machine training first, but the prompt is only a request to the model, and in testing it sometimes skips the check. The check must run on every booking without exception. Which change guarantees it?

options.text: Add a bold line to the prompt telling the model never to skip the check
Switch to a larger model so that it is less likely to skip any step
Make the check a fixed code step that runs before any booking is saved
Give the model a worked example of a booking that includes the check
